# 4. Play a character, and make the character believable and developed.
The server standards are for an MRP+ environment. Story is encouraged more than gameplay. Your character is not, and should not, be the main character. Rounds consist of the actions of dozens of separate people influencing the station at large - interact with others and create engaging moments. Characters can and should have unique and interesting moments, the story doesn’t revolve around them, though.
Make sure your character’s name is believable: they were hired onto a reputable station’s staff. Follow the recommendations for species naming in the guidebook, players of any species can use any species naming conventions.
If your character was hired on as a cargo technician, would they know how to synthesize every chemical just because you, the player, knows how? Would a character hired on as a janitor be aware of how to set up a tesla or singularity? Play into your character’s fields of knowledge, avoid the want to have your characters be good at everything. It’s more fun and engaging for everyone to let certain characters in rounds have the expertise and spotlight!
There are many dangers to life on a space station: you should value your life and overall well being. Most chefs would not be the one to run into action against 3 very armed terrorists, or try to perform a citizen’s arrest on a dangerous, cosmically ascended cultist.
## Allowed - A human Warden named “Jonathan W. Cage”, where the W. is short for Will. - A Mothperson raised by slimes called “Blimpuf Blyumpson”. - A scientist refusing to help Security fight Nukies because they were hired for science research.
## Not Allowed - A human Warden named “John Warden”. - A red-frilled lizardperson named “Chappell Roan”. - A cargo tech ordering 4 crates of shotguns and single handedly taking down every revolutionary on station wordlessly.
